description: REQ-E5's trust anchor `spawn-surface.pinned.json` is itself NOT covered by any of the three protection layers it establishes for the files it pins, creating a self-reference loop that defeats the entire ROUND-2-002 closure. Concretely: REQ-E5 at lines 357-361 enumerates the spawn surface as exactly five files (`adversary-daily.sh`, `adversary-daily-prompt.tmpl`, `loop-improve.py`, `payout-endpoint-allowlist.json`, `hook-modules-allowlist.txt`). `spawn-surface.pinned.json` is conspicuously absent from this list. Then: (1) the startup sha256 check at lines 369-372 reads expected hashes FROM `spawn-surface.pinned.json` and compares against the five surface files — it cannot self-verify because the file containing the expected hashes is itself the only source of truth, so any tampering with pinned.json is invisible to the runtime check; (2) the OS-level immutability clause at lines 374-378 requires `0444 + chflags uchg` only for files in `REQ-C3`/`REQ-E2`/`loop-propose`'s write target list — pinned.json is explicitly not described as a spawn-surface file, so it is not in scope of this protection; (3) the adversary string-match gate at lines 380-382 only scans `strategy.json.next` for spawn-surface paths — pinned.json is not in that list either. The only declared protection is the prose claim at lines 363-367 that pinned.json is 'updated ONLY by a tagged commit on main (signed off in the commit message body with the literal token SPAWN-SURFACE-PIN-UPDATE)' — but the spec defines NO enforcement mechanism for this rule (no Git pre-commit hook, no pre-receive hook, no signed-tag verification, no CI gate). A pass running under REQ-C3 strategy mutation, or `loop-improve.py` auto-fix, or `loop-propose.sh` import, can: (a) rewrite the five surface files to a malicious version, (b) recompute their sha256 values, (c) rewrite pinned.json with the new hashes, (d) every subsequent startup check now reads the malicious-but-self-consistent pinned.json and reports OK. The 'three layers' the spec advertises collapse to ZERO when pinned.json is the corruption target. PROP-E5-spawn-pin fixture corpus also does NOT include a 'pinned.json itself was rewritten' attack, so the verification obligation does not catch this. Required fix (any one is sufficient): (i) add pinned.json to the spawn-surface list AND store a separate sha256 of pinned.json itself in a place outside the surface (e.g. baked into `loop-healthcheck.sh` source as a constant, or in a separate `pinned.json.meta-pin` file with its own chflags uchg), AND require startup to verify pinned.json against that out-of-band anchor before reading the inner pins; (ii) require a Git server-side `pre-receive` hook on the anicca repo that rejects any push touching `spawn-surface.pinned.json` unless the most recent commit message contains the `SPAWN-SURFACE-PIN-UPDATE` token AND is signed with a key in a CI-managed allowlist — and require this hook itself to be part of the spawn surface; (iii) move pinned.json out of the self-mutating tree entirely (e.g. into a separate immutable bucket like a notarized Apple-signed plist or a write-once log) and reference it by an out-of-band path. As specified, the spec describes a wall around a vault and forgets to lock the front door.

evidence.snippet: THE SYSTEM SHALL maintain `~/anicca/skills/_shared/spawn-surface.pinned.json` containing the sha256 of each spawn-surface file at the most recent human-signed release. This file is updated ONLY by a tagged commit on `main` (signed off in the commit message body with the literal token `SPAWN-SURFACE-PIN-UPDATE`); it is NEVER updated by REQ-C3 strategy mutation, REQ-C2 improve, REQ-E2 builder auto-fix, or REQ-loop-propose imports. ... ANY mismatch SHALL halt the script before any side effect AND call `escalate.sh <slot> spawn-surface-drift ...`.
